title: Memory with Onsager-Casimir symmetry: Rotating particle in a viscoelastic fluid
authors: Debankur Das, Niloyendu Roy, Niklas Windbacher, Clemens Bechinger, Matthias Krüger
abstract: We study the stochastic dynamics of a rotating Brownian particle in a non-Markovian fluid. Experimentally, we find that rotation enhances the long-time diffusivity of the particle and generates time-antisymmetric cross-correlations between orthogonal displacement components in the plane perpendicular to the rotation axis. To rationalize these observations, we introduce a minimal linear model in which a tracer is coupled to a slow bath degree of freedom and rotation enters through an advective coupling. Eliminating the bath variable yields a generalized Langevin equation with a non-reciprocal memory kernel. This kernel rotates in time, forming a logarithmic spiral, and it obeys Onsager-Casimir symmetry under reversal of the rotation vector, and the corresponding fluctuation-response relation. From the latter we obtain a geometric construction that links two-time cross-correlations to the transverse response of the particle in bulk. Unlike the ordinary Einstein relation, this relation involves the antisymmetric sector of the response. Our experiments and theory are in qualitative agreement, establishing rotating colloids in viscoelastic fluids as a minimal realization of Onsager-Casimir symmetry in time-nonlocal stochastic dynamics
summary: This work analyzes the motion of a rotating particle in a viscoelastic fluid, finding that rotation introduces non-Markovian effects and breaks time-reversal symmetry. By developing a theoretical model based on generalized Langevin equations, the authors establish that this system serves as a minimal physical realization demonstrating Onsager–Casimir symmetry in complex stochastic dynamics.
main_problem: The study investigates the stochastic dynamics of a rotating Brownian particle in a non-Markovian, viscoelastic fluid to understand how rotation breaks time-reversal symmetry beyond standard fluctuation-dissipation relations.
main_result: Rotation induces enhanced long-time diffusivity and generates time-antisymmetric cross-correlations, establishing the system as a minimal realization of Onsager–Casimir symmetry in time-nonlocal stochastic dynamics.
method: The authors use a minimal linear model coupling the particle to a bath variable, deriving a generalized Langevin equation with a non-reciprocal memory kernel and analyzing fluctuation correlations.
model_or_system: The system is a superparamagnetic colloidal particle rotating in a viscoelastic fluid. The dynamics are modeled using coupled Langevin equations involving an advective coupling term that breaks time-reversal symmetry.
key_observables: Enhanced long-time diffusivity, time-antisymmetric cross-correlations ($C_{ij}(t, t') = -C_{ij}(t', t)$), and the Magnus effect.
important_parameters: Rotation frequency ($\Omega$), viscoelastic fluid properties (related to memory kernel decay rates $k$ and $\gamma$).
main_assumptions: The advective coupling term is phenomenological, and the analysis relies on deriving generalized fluctuation-dissipation relations for non-Markovian noise.
figures_summary: Figures show schematic setups, Magnus effect trajectories, MSD vs. rotation frequency (showing enhancement), and cross-correlation components demonstrating antisymmetry.
paper_structure: The paper progresses from experimental observation of enhanced diffusion and asymmetry to developing a minimal theoretical model involving coupled Langevin equations, deriving the non-reciprocal memory kernel, and finally establishing the generalized Onsager–Casimir symmetry relation connecting correlations to transverse response.
why_interesting: It provides an accessible physical realization (colloids in viscoelastic fluids) for studying fundamental symmetries like Onsager-Casimir relations in complex, time-nonlocal stochastic dynamics, which has parallels in open quantum systems theory.
